MOD = 10**9 + 7

def countPalindromicPaths(matrix):
    n = len(matrix)
    m = len(matrix[0])
    
    # dp[i][j] will store the number of palindromic paths ending at (i, j)
    dp = [[[0] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)] for _ in range(m + 1)]
    
    # Base case: there's one way to be at the start (top-left corner)
    dp[1][1][1] = 1
    
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            for k in range(1, m + 1):
                if i > 1:
                    dp[i][j][k] += dp[i - 1][j][k]
                if j > 1:
                    dp[i][j][k] += dp[i][j - 1][k]
                if k > 1:
                    dp[i][j][k] += dp[i][j][k - 1]
                
                dp[i][j][k] %= MOD
                
                # Check if the path from (1, 1) to (i, j) is a palindrome
                if matrix[i - 1][j - 1] == matrix[k - 1][j - 1]:
                    dp[i][j][k] += dp[i][j][k - 1]
                    dp[i][j][k] %= MOD
    
    return dp[n][m][m]
